title: The utility of lifting gear
summary: NH sorts lifting gear into items that keep form tight (belts) and items that store elastic energy (sleeves, wraps, bench shirts, slingshots), with straps in a class of their own. Gear is legitimate and good for longevity when used for real reasons, not fashion or to cover bad form, though it can shift stress to unprotected areas.
claims: Most gear either keeps form tight or stores kinetic energy; straps are their own category
Keeping posture tight lets you use your full musculature; in a squat, a rounding back takes the legs out and turns it into a good morning
A belt doesn't store energy; it adds rigidity so you don't fold, letting you develop power
Elastic gear has a learning curve; a bench shirt on a beginner can stop them touching their chest
Knee sleeves and basic wraps add poundage for almost anyone; long knee wraps need practice
A belt takes some lower back stress and arguably makes legs work more by enabling leg drive
Any effect of a belt on ab use is too small to matter for hypertrophy
There's no shame using a belt if you've built a reassuring connection with it, as long as it doesn't hide bad form
Sleeves and wraps double up on tendons: they keep them warm, stop grinding and thicken the joint
Thicker joints give bigger strength potential, so wraps help those with small wrists or knees
Using gear for fashion, like the 2016 slingshot trend, is useless; it should fit your program, recovery and goals
No equipment will save a tendon or disc if your form puts enough stress on it
A belt does nothing for the SI joint; many 'belted deadlift back injuries' are SI joint injuries from the extra intensity
Gear can protect one area while shifting stress to another
After snapping his knee, cheap elastic wraps placed over the weak part of the tendon helped him most
He uses wrist and elbow wraps to keep everything tight and pain-free
Even a placebo effect from gear is still an effect
Do warm-up sets raw and add gear from about 75-80% intensity; don't belt up for one plate
He used a belt once, didn't like it, and never used one again
Refusing gear out of dogma is the real ego lifting; using it for longevity shows humility
exercises: rigidity; protects lower back, not SI joint
warm tendons, thicker joint, store energy
he uses them for pain-free training
